courses.title: Intermediate Chinese I
courses.description: [GE 3B] Expansion of the first year of Mandarin Chinese. Continuation of the development of the four language skills of aurally understanding, speaking, reading and writing within a cultural context. Increasing sophistication of grammatical constructions and more advanced vocabulary.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 173, CHN 1112 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Intermediate Chinese II
courses.description: [GE 3B] Continuation of Intermediate Chinese I. Further development of the four language skills within a cultural context. Practice of spoken and written Mandarin Chinese in communicative activities. Introduction of more advanced grammatical structures needed to perform various functional tasks.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 271, CHN 2111 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Intermediate Chinese III
courses.description: [GE 3B] Continuation of Intermediate Mandarin Chinese II. Further expansion and integration of the four language skills within a cultural context. Development of idioms and more advanced grammar. Emphasis on language proficiency and social skills in various communicative tasks.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 271, CHN 2112 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Chinese Civilization and Culture
courses.description: Comprehensive interdisciplinary study of Chinese civilizational heritage and cultural traditions from comparative perspectives with a focused reading of primary texts (in Chinese original and/or English translation) and scholarly works in philosophy, literature, art and other subjects related to Chinese civilization and culture.

courses.title: Chinese Civilization and Culture
courses.description: [GE 3C] Comprehensive study of Chinese civilizational heritage and cultural traditions from cross-cultural and interdisciplinary perspectives. Reading and discussion focus on Chinese philosophy, literature, art, and sciences to achieve an in-depth synthetic understanding of China’s past and present. The course is taught in English.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: China to 1127
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to Chinese history from the earliest historical writings to the fall of the Northern Song dynasty, focusing on archeological origins, rise of the textual tradition, development of political and economic institutions, elite culture, philosophical traditions, social institutions, and religion.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: China 1127-1644
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to Chinese history from the Southern Song Dynasty through Mongol rule and into consolidation of late imperial China. Changes and continuities in Chinese political, social, cultural, and economic institutions and thought. Chinese border relations.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: China 1644-1927
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to late imperial China and the transition to a modern nation-state under Republican China. Focus on Manchu rule, reform and revolution, material culture, changing male and female identities, society and social changes, warlord states, and intellectual developments.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.
